title: A Genius With Amnesia - Victor Savkin, Nx
talk_summary: Victor Savkin argues agents are 'geniuses with amnesia': repo-bound (can't see the whole system) and session-bound (no episodic memory), forcing humans to re-explain one change up to seven times across repos. Nx's Polygraph is a meta-harness that builds a cross-repo dependency graph and captures full session state/traces so any agent can resume any work on any machine, treating multi-repo changes as one.

takeaways.technique: Persist and replay full session state/traces, not just a summary
takeaways.what_they_do: Capture intent, repos, PRs, and all agent traces per session; store them so a session can be materialized on another machine with the same SHAs and history, and any agent can resume it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We also capture all agent traces... all of that lets us restore any session, any piece of work on any machine

takeaways.technique: Cross-repo dependency graph as agent context
takeaways.what_they_do: Analyze repos out-of-band to extract what each project produces/consumes (packages, APIs) and stitch into one graph, giving the agent an illusion of one big codebase it can read/write anywhere.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can analyze them and extract a lot of metadata out of them to build unified dependency graph
takeaways.numbers: ~300 owned repos + thousands of OSS repos in one personal graph

takeaways.technique: Treat multi-repo CI as one vector with attribution
takeaways.what_they_do: When CI fails in any repo of a session, the harness determines whether the consumer needs a patch or the producer is broken and incompatible, then routes the fix to the right agent(s).
takeaways.evidence_quote: if module one fails within a polygraph session, it will figure out who fixes it, whether module one needed a patch or the UI component itself is broken

takeaways.what_they_do: A single agent session can check out and modify several repos, producing coordinated PRs, so the change is explained once and applied consistently everywhere.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I explained the change once and I got it implemented in both repos and it's all in agreement
takeaways.numbers: 7 explanations collapsed to 1 for a single change

takeaways.technique: Resume the author's session to review
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking the author, a reviewer resumes their session, gets exact state and traces, and queries the agent about decisions made.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I resume their session on my machine, I get the exact state, fully functional, zero setup, and then I just talk to my agent about the decisions

takeaways.technique: Agent-agnostic harness enables mid-session model swap
takeaways.what_they_do: Because state lives in the harness, not the agent, you can switch from one model to another mid-session when one goes down.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is also useful when I want to switch from say Claude to Codex mid-session when something goes down
